title: Incremental hosted surface PRD: scope adjustments, compatibility shims, and launch steps for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Define a minimal, incremental PRD to align product, engineering, and design on a compact hostable API behavior for chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank endpoints. This ticket focuses on scope adjustments to avoid large-surface rewrites, compatibility shims for existing customers, and a concrete launch checklist for a phased rollout. Objective is to reduce ambiguity in acceptance criteria and minimize regression risk for customers relying on prior endpoint semantics.
goals: Define a clear behavior contract for hosted chat/completions/embeddings/rerank that is backward-compatible for 90% of current customers
Document scope changes compared to the full consolidation plan and identify work that will be deferred
Provide a deterministic launch checklist and gating criteria so Eng and DX can validate readiness
Create a compatibility shim plan for SDKs and server-side routing to avoid breaking customers during rollout
outcomes: Signed-off acceptance criteria and test plan for API behavior
Engineering execution tickets prioritizing compatibility shims and telemetry
A rollout runbook with canary thresholds and rollback triggers
SDK compatibility matrix and migration notes for customers
in_scope: Behavioral spec for generation endpoints: chat and completions (prompt handling, default temperature/penalties, streaming semantics)
Embedding vector response format and versioning rules
Rerank endpoint expected request/response contract and scoring normalization
Compatibility shims: header-based routing flag to enable new behavior per-customer or per-route
Acceptance tests and telemetry dashboards for quality/regression detection
out_of_scope: Full API surface consolidation (deeper refactor to merge chat/completions into a single API) - deferred to next quarter
Major SDK redesigns beyond compatibility wrappers
Dedicated capacity autoscaling changes and private deployment packaging
requirements: REQ-01: Provide a single authoritative behavioral spec doc for each endpoint (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank)
REQ-02: Implement header flag X-RI-API-MODE to toggle new behavior path for canary customers
REQ-03: Ensure streaming chunk boundaries are identical to existing hosted semantics unless header toggled
REQ-04: Embedding responses must include embedding_version field and consistent length for model families
REQ-05: Rerank responses must return normalized scores in [0,1] and documented tie-breaking behavior
REQ-06: Add evaluation prompt set for regression detection (per-endpoint minimal suite)
REQ-07: Create SDK compatibility wrappers for JS and Python that set header by default until migration opt-in
acceptance_criteria: AC-01: Behavioral spec published and approved by PM, Eng, and Design (signatures in doc)
AC-02: Compatibility header implemented and honored by routing layer; unit/integration tests covering both legacy and new paths
AC-03: Regression evals pass baseline quality thresholds (no >5% drop in top-1 accuracy for rerank; embedding cosine shift within tolerated delta) for canary dataset
AC-04: SDK wrappers released to npm/pypi with migration guide and deprecation timeline noted
AC-05: Observatory dashboards show token-level cost, latency P50/P95, and quality metrics for canary traffic; thresholds defined and monitored
AC-06: Runbook contains explicit rollback steps and runbook tested in staging with a simulated canary failure
launch_checklist: Checklist-01: Prod behavior spec PDF uploaded to Confluence and linked from console feature page
Checklist-02: ENG: Header flag implemented + feature toggle in deployment pipeline
Checklist-03: DES: SDK wrapper UX copy and example snippets reviewed and approved
Checklist-04: DX/Docs: Migration guide and changelog entry published; update FAQ for common breaking scenarios
Checklist-05: QE: Regression suites for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank added to CI and green for two consecutive runs
Checklist-06: Observability: Dashboards and alerting configured (latency, error-rate, model-quality drift) with alert-owners
Checklist-07: Legal & Security: Basic data handling review completed for the header toggle path
Checklist-08: Release comms: Email and in-product banner drafts ready for canary participants
Checklist-09: Canary launch scheduled with percent and region plan (start 1% global traffic -> 5% -> 20%)
Checklist-10: Post-launch review slated (operation review + quality report) 7 days after 20% ramp
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Staging): Run full acceptance tests against staging models; simulate network failures and verify rollback steps
Phase 1 (Canary internal): Route internal traffic (10% of non-customer API tokens) with header enabled for 48 hours
Phase 2 (External canary): Invite 5-8 power customers and opt them into header flag; monitor QA metrics for 72 hours
Phase 3 (Gradual ramp): 1% -> 5% -> 20% over 72-96 hours with stop-and-evaluate gates at each step
Phase 4 (Full launch): Remove header opt-in and flip default once quality thresholds and SLA targets are met for 7 consecutive days
risks_mitigations: Risk: Unexpected quality regressions for rerank leading to customer complaints. Mitigation: Hold back critical enterprise customers and run backfill evaluation on their telemetry before ramp.
Risk: SDK adoption lag causing confusion. Mitigation: Provide automatic header behavior in SDK wrappers and clear migration timeline with code samples.
Risk: Latency regression due to additional routing checks. Mitigation: Benchmark routing path and add micro-optimized hot path for header-disabled requests.
Risk: Edge case breaking streaming consumers. Mitigation: Add streaming compatibility tests and provide streaming-interpreter fallback in the shim
metrics: Metric-1: Top-1 rerank precision on canary dataset (target: within -5% of baseline)
Metric-2: Embedding cosine similarity drift vs baseline (target: <0.02 average shift)
Metric-3: API latency P95 change (target: <+15ms absolute)
Metric-4: Error rate introduced by header path (target: <0.1% increase)
Metric-5: SDK adoption % (target: 30% of active JS/Python users opt into wrapper within 30 days)
Metric-6: Customer support tickets attributable to this launch (target: <10 in first 7 days)
implementation_notes: Use header X-RI-API-MODE values: legacy | incremental | experimental; default remains legacy until full flip
Ensure model-version tagging in responses for easier debugging (response field: model_tag)
Keep streaming chunk delimiter unchanged for legacy path; experimental can include structured break tokens
Provide an API response field migration_hint explaining differences when incremental mode is returned
